outcome: breech presentation (as an outcome when investigating predictors)
adverse delivery outcome (cesarean section or other obstetrical interventions)
adverse fetal outcomes (Apgar score <= 7, need for perinatal intensive treatment, intrauterine death, perinatal mortality)
cohort: All term (>= 37 weeks), singleton pregnancies with cephalic and breech presentation in Hungary between 1996-2011, totaling 41,796 participants.
finding: Breech presentation is independently associated with an increased risk of gestational complications, including adverse delivery outcomes (11.7 times more frequent) and adverse fetal outcomes (1.39 times more frequent, 1.18 after adjustment) compared with cephalic presentation.
mod_finding: An adverse delivery outcome, which included cesarean section or other obstetrical interventions at birth, was 11.7 times more frequent in pregnancies with breech presentation compared with cephalic presentation.
birth_weight: Birthweight was analyzed as a fetal factor associated with breech presentation and small for gestational age was also considered.
gest_age: Term pregnancies (>= 37 weeks) were included, and younger gestational age at delivery was identified as a predictor of breech presentation.
